residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Alberta for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The 1-year separation must be completed before or by the time the application is granted. Divorce Order effective 31 days after made (Divorce Act, s.12).

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: Respondent has treated applicant with physical or mental cruelty rendering cohabitation intolerable.

terminology.maritalProperty: Family Property (Family Property Act, RSA 2000, c. F-4.7)

filingFees.notes: Fee waiver available for low-income parties. Court of King's Bench has jurisdiction (rebranded from Queen's Bench in 2022).

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply in all provinces. Alberta enforces through the Maintenance Enforcement Program (MEP).

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only — not legislatively mandated but widely applied by Alberta courts

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce judgment is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Judgment (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).
notes: Alberta uses 'family property' with a presumption of equal division (Family Property Act, s.7). Court of King's Bench of Alberta has exclusive jurisdiction over divorce. Judicial districts include Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Lethbridge, and others.
